newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin to convert bonds, share slips.
newsitem.headline: Michelin to convert bonds, share slips.

text.p: Tyremaker Michelin said on Monday it would redeem 3.5 billion francs of convertible bonds into shares ahead of schedule, the second such operation in less than six months.
Last October it announced plans to redeem 1.5 billion francs of convertible bonds.

Analysts welcomed the redemptions, which they said would reduce Michelin's debt by around five billion francs, but the share closed down 1.29 percent at 337.20 francs after a rise of 18 percent since the beginning of the year.
One analyst said Monday's drop was due to sales of Michelin shares by fund managers seeking to maintain the proportion of equities to other instruments in their portfolios.
At the end of June 1996, Michelin's debt, including subordinated debt, stood at 23.2 billion francs for a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.97.
The company said last month that it aimed to reach its "ideal" debt-to-equity ratio of between one and 1.3 soon.

One analyst said the convertible bond redemptions would help the tyremaker reach its objective this year. He said he expected the group's debt to fall to 17 billion francs at the end of 1997 for a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.67.
A month ago, U.S. brokerage Merrill Lynch upgraded its recommendation on the Michelin's stock, saying the market was not taking into account "how quickly Michelin is throwing off (its) debt burden".
Michelin has been struggling to bring down its debt since its acquisition seven years ago of Uniroyal Goodrich of the United States.
Michelin said in a financial advertisement that it would retire its 2.50 percent convertible bonds maturing in the year 2001 on March 21 at terms which analysts called very attractive.

The bonds are redeemable for 277.77 francs. On February 12, the conversion parity was 1.01 B shares for each convertible bond, it said, adding that those shares were last traded on the bourse at 336 francs.
